obtained.how: abstract only: the USGS Publications Warehouse record (pubs.usgs.gov publication 1000168, Great Lakes Science Center), read through its JSON service; no full text there or anywhere else found

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref (the SICI DOI resolves there when URL-encoded) and the USGS record
bibliography.note: Edsall, Thomas A. 1970 (April). Trans. Am. Fish. Soc. 99(2): 376–380. show.mjs's 'DOI NOT FOUND at Crossref' is an encoding artefact: the encoded DOI resolves.

claims.claim: hatch spread over 13 d at 7.8 °C, 2–3 d at 20–21 °C
claims.note: Abstract only. The abstract gives the 'time from start to finish of hatching' as 13 days at about 46 °F (7.8 °C) and 2–3 days at 68–70 °F (20.0–21.1 °C); the paper's conversions are right.

claims.paper: Table 3.6-1 (sea-run alewife, hatch and first feeding)
claims.claim: unfed larvae live 3.8 d at 10.6 °C, 7.6 d at 14.4–15 °C, 2.4 d at 26.7–27.8 °C
claims.note: Abstract only. The abstract gives survival of unfed larvae held at their incubation temperatures as 3.8 d at 51 °F, 7.6 d at 58–59 °F and 2.4 d at 80–82 °F; the conversions (10.6, 14.4–15.0, 26.7–27.8 °C) are right. Whether these are mean or maximum survival times needs the full text.

claims.claim: the best hatch in the research is 38 %, in the laboratory near 17.8 °C
claims.note: Abstract only (the paper already says 'abstract only'). The abstract gives the optimum as 38 % hatched at about 64 °F (17.8 °C), from eggs incubated at 79 constant temperatures between 42.1 and 87.0 °F; hatching happened at 44.4–84.9 °F.

claims.claim: the best hatch is 38 % in the lab near 17.8 °C ('Edsall 1970 via Fay'), the basis for hatch 0.2
claims.note: As for §5.2. The comment says 'via Fay', while the research note (sea_run_alewife.md) took it from the USGS abstract; either way the full text was not read.

notes: For the rewrite: Edsall's eggs came from LANDLOCKED Lake Michigan alewives, while Table 3.6-1's row and §5.2 are about the sea-run alewife. The table should say so (e.g. 'Lake Michigan alewife eggs, laboratory'). The 38 % is a laboratory optimum across a temperature gradient, not a field hatch rate; §5.2 already frames it that way. The abstract also gives incubation times (15 d at 45 °F, 3.7 d at 70 °F, 2.1 d at 84 °F) that the research note's incubation fit uses. All claims stay unchecked until the full text (TAFS 99:376–380) is fetched by hand.
